title: Impact of Upwind Pollution on Infant Mortality

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Instrumental Variables (IV / 2SLS)**

The research question asks whether pollution exposure (x) causally affects infant mortality (y). OLS estimation of this relationship is likely biased due to endogeneity — pollution exposure correlates with unobserved factors (e.g., poverty, industrial activity, healthcare access) that independently affect infant mortality.

**Instrument:** Wind direction (z), specifically whether the pollution source is upwind (z=1) or not (z=0).

**Key assumptions:**
1. **Relevance:** Wind direction (upwind pollution source) significantly affects local pollution exposure levels. This is testable via the first-stage F-statistic.
2. **Exclusion restriction:** Wind direction affects infant mortality *only* through its effect on pollution exposure, not through any other channel. This is plausible since wind direction is essentially a quasi-random meteorological phenomenon, unlikely to directly affect infant health except through pollution transport.
3. **Independence:** Wind direction is as-good-as-randomly assigned conditional on controls — it should be uncorrelated with unobserved determinants of infant mortality.

## 2. R Code

```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)       # ivreg for 2SLS
library(lmtest)    # coeftest
library(sandwich)  # robust SEs

# ─── Read Data ───
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s75_data.csv")
cat("Dataset dimensions:", nrow(df), "obs x", ncol(df), "vars\n\n")
summary(df)

# ─── Step 1: OLS (Naive) Estimation ───
cat("\n========== OLS (Naive) Estimation ==========\n")
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
summary(ols_model)
cat("OLS coefficient on pollution (x):", coef(ols_model)["x"], "\n\n")

# ─── Step 2: First Stage ───
cat("========== First Stage: x ~ z + controls ==========\n")
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
summary(first_stage)

# First-stage F-statistic for instrument strength
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic
f_value <- f_stat[1]
f_pval <- pf(f_stat[1], f_stat[2], f_stat[3], lower.tail = FALSE)
cat("First-stage F-statistic:", f_value, "\n")
cat("First-stage p-value:", f_pval, "\n")
cat("Instrument relevance (F > 10 rule of thumb):", ifelse(f_value > 10, "PASS", "WEAK"), "\n\n")

# Coefficient on z in first stage
cat("First-stage coefficient on z (upwind):", coef(first_stage)["z"], "\n\n")

# ─── Step 3: IV / 2SLS Estimation ───
cat("========== IV / 2SLS Estimation ==========\n")
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)

# Robust standard errors
cat("\n--- IV with Robust Standard Errors ---\n")
robust_iv <- coeftest(iv_model, vcov = vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_iv)

cat("\nIV coefficient on pollution (x):", coef(iv_model)["x"], "\n")
cat("OLS coefficient on pollution (x):", coef(ols_model)["x"], "\n")
cat("Difference (IV - OLS):", coef(iv_model)["x"] - coef(ols_model)["x"], "\n\n")

# ─── Step 4: Reduced Form ───
cat("========== Reduced Form: y ~ z + controls ==========\n")
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
summary(reduced_form)
cat("Reduced-form coefficient on z:", coef(reduced_form)["z"], "\n")
cat("Implied IV (reduced form / first stage):", 
    coef(reduced_form)["z"] / coef(first_stage)["z"], "\n\n")

# ─── Step 5: Robustness Checks ───
cat("========== Robustness Checks ==========\n\n")

# 5a: IV without controls
cat("--- IV without controls ---\n")
iv_no_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
summary(iv_no_controls)
cat("IV (no controls) coefficient on x:", coef(iv_no_controls)["x"], "\n\n")

# 5b: Check balance — is z correlated with controls?
cat("--- Balance check: controls ~ z ---\n")
balance_test <- lm(controls ~ z, data = df)
summary(balance_test)
cat("Coefficient of z on controls:", coef(balance_test)["z"], 
    " (p =", summary(balance_test)$coefficients["z", "Pvalue"], ")\n")
cat("If insignificant, supports instrument exogeneity.\n\n")

# 5c: Wu-Hausman test for endogeneity
cat("--- Wu-Hausman Endogeneity Test ---\n")
first_stage_resid <- residuals(first_stage)
hausman_test <- lm(y ~ x + controls + first_stage_resid, data = df)
cat("Coefficient on first-stage residuals:", coef(hausman_test)["first_stage_resid"], "\n")
cat("p-value:", summary(hausman_test)$coefficients["first_stage_resid", "Pr(>|t|)"], "\n")
cat("If significant, endogeneity is present and IV is preferred over OLS.\n\n")

# ─── Summary Table ───
cat("========== SUMMARY ==========\n")
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10s %10s\n", "Method", "Coef(x)", "SE"))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f\n", "OLS", 
            coef(ols_model)["x"], summary(ols_model)$coefficients["x","Std. Error"]))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f\n", "IV/2SLS", 
            coef(iv_model)["x"], summary(iv_model)$coefficients["x","Std. Error"]))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f\n", "IV (no controls)", 
            coef(iv_no_controls)["x"], summary(iv_no_controls)$coefficients["x","Std. Error"]))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign:** **Positive** — higher pollution exposure should increase infant mortality rates.

**Magnitude considerations:**
- The IV estimate is expected to be **larger in absolute magnitude** than the OLS estimate. OLS likely suffers from attenuation bias (measurement error in pollution exposure) and possibly omitted variable bias that could bias the OLS coefficient toward zero or even make it negative (if wealthier, lower-mortality areas happen to have more monitored/reported pollution).
- The IV captures the **Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE)** — the causal effect of pollution for the subpopulation whose exposure is influenced by wind direction (compliers).

**First stage:** I expect z (upwind indicator) to positively and significantly predict pollution exposure (x), with an F-statistic well above 10, confirming instrument relevance.

**Reduced form:** The coefficient of z on y should be positive (upwind pollution source → higher infant mortality), and dividing by the first-stage coefficient should recover the IV estimate.

**Robustness:** The Wu-Hausman test should likely indicate endogeneity is present (justifying IV over OLS). The balance check should show z is uncorrelated with socioeconomic controls, supporting the exclusion restriction's plausibility. Results should be stable across specifications with and without controls.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Wind direction is used as an instrument for pollution exposure.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Upwind pollution exposure is found to significantly increase infant mortality.
